nodes.text: Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}$ be the sequence of powerful numbers (if $p\mid n$ then $p^2\mid n$). Are there only finitely many three-term progressions of consecutive terms $n_k,n_{k+1},n_{k+2}$?

#938 : [Er76d] number theory | powerful Erdős also conjectured (see [364] ) that there are no triples of powerful numbers of the shape $n,n+1,n+2$.
